pages.text: The total saturation of the dishes decides how many guests will come, while their variety and quality decide whether a rare guest is willing to come.$(br2)The higher a dish's saturation, the more appeal it carries, and appeal decides the quality of the gift after the meal. Note that the same dish only ever counts once toward appeal.

Every guest has her own threshold. A single cake is enough to invite Cirno, while Suika wants a grand buffet.$(br2)You can put out more food partway through; once a guest has eaten her fill, her pace drops sharply and she may leave early.$(br2)Aim the invitation letter at the table nearest the centre, or the farther tables may see no visitors; the number of seats decides how many guests can come at once.

Higher favour will not bring a guest who does not qualify; it only raises the share of those who do.$(br2)After the meal every guest leaves a gift, and its quality depends on the appeal of the food she ate.
